body:
Prompt injection risk (source): content/job-processor.js extracts schema.org JobPosting.description from untrusted web pages and stores it in the job info object. If forwarded into Gemini prompts downstream, malicious job content can inject instructions; current handling strips tags but does not provide a deterministic prompt-injection control. --- To fix this without changing core functionality, strengthen stripLdHtml so it does **both**: (1) preserve useful job-description text and (2) deterministically neutralize common prompt-injection instruction patterns before the text is stored in job info.

Best single fix in this file:

  • Edit content/job-processor.js, function stripLdHtml (around lines 225–231).
  • Keep existing HTML stripping and whitespace normalization.
  • Add targeted regex-based redaction of common instruction-like phrases used in prompt injection (e.g., “ignore previous instructions”, “system prompt”, “developer message”, “do not follow above”, “reveal hidden prompt”, etc.).
  • Add explicit length capping in this function (or keep existing downstream cap) so oversized payloads are bounded deterministically at source.
  • Return cleaned text string as before, so existing callers remain compatible.

No new imports or dependencies are required.
